title_options: Your Agent Drops 380 KB of Tool Output. Which Line Survives?
Truncation Policy at the Tool Boundary: A Survival Matrix for Agent Tool Results
Head, Tail or Match-Centred: Choosing an Agent's Tool-Output Cap
presentation.title_rationale: The reader problem is a tool result that the harness silently cuts; the title names the dropped volume measured in this article (380,110 of 400,110 characters) and the single supported benefit - knowing which line survives under which policy - without claiming a fix, and it moves methods, budget and year into the subtitle and introduction.
presentation.visual_purpose: A 5x5 survival matrix drawn only from part_a_results.json: rows are the five policies, columns the five evidence positions, filled cells the positions where the planted evidence line survived. It shows the geometry (each position-blind rule wins at most 2 of 5) rather than a decorative concept; no invented values, no model output.

numbers.note: Every figure (400,110; 20,000; 20,014; 0.067 s; spans; 1/5..5/5) is copied from part_a_results.json or computed from it; 380 KB is 380,110 chars.

claims.note: The 380 KB in the headline is 400,110 minus the 20,000-char budget = 380,110 chars dropped (95.0%), from the first-party run; the 'which line survives' promise is the measured matrix, not a model claim.
Editorial framing of the reader problem. The 62% example illustrates a position outside a head cap; it is not a measured case and is not attributed to a study.

Vendor source and docs read at the pinned tag/commit on 2026-11-22: Ollama chatPrompt front-drops messages and defaults to 4096 tokens; Codex splits a byte/token budget half per end with the marker outside the budget and approximates 4 bytes per token. The 'no tool message of that size can be carried' sentence is arithmetic (100,000 tokens vs a 4096-token default), not a measured run.
Fixture construction as implemented in build_payload(): deterministic log lines to 400,000 chars plus one planted evidence line snapped to a line boundary. Verbatim from the published script.

claims.note: Arithmetic on the fixture geometry only: the 20,000-char budget is 5.0% of the 400,110-char payload (20,000/400,110 = 4.9986%) and a doubled 40,000-char cap is 10.0% (40,000/400,110 = 9.9973%), so the evidence line at 62% (248,068 chars) stays outside either cap. No new measurement is claimed; the figures are ratios of the measured payload_chars_first in part_a_results.json.
Explicit statement of what the deterministic matrix does not measure, including that no model was called and no accuracy ranking is claimed.
Limitations of the fixture: synthetic uniform-line payload, character rather than token budgets, one budget and one payload size.
Advisory rule derived from the measured geometry; the regex class and the head-cap fallback are recommendations, not measured outcomes.

Codex emits a marker naming the removed count and documents the marker as outside the retained-text budget; the silent-cap contrast is a characterisation of a bare slice, not a claim about a named implementation.
Interpretive paragraph about where the budget decision is made; makes no factual claim beyond the table.

The three published files exist in the evidence directory and are linked by post-publication raw GitHub URL, listed in public_artifacts with hashes; the 143-line count and 0.07 s runtime are from truncation_survival.py and the observed elapsed_s.
States plainly that the model arm was not run and that no policy ranking by answer accuracy is claimed; the planned design is described as a plan, not a result.
Contextual links to sibling articles; characterises their scope without quoting numbers from them.

corrections.disclosure_for_reviewer: One wording observation was left unchanged in the article body because the correction scope says the body needs no change, and it is disclosed here so the reviewer can rule on it: the article writes Codex "is explicit that 'the marker is outside the retained-text budget'", in quotation marks. The pinned source comment reads "Retain at most `max_bytes` from a string's ends and add a character-count marker outside that budget" (codex-rs/utils/string/src/truncate.rs, lines 42-44 at 104d256). The meaning matches; the exact string does not, so the quoted phrase is a paraphrase. Receipt claim 15 already labels this as a characterisation. Verified in this correction run against the freshly re-fetched, byte-identical snapshot.

changed.was: Doubling the cap to 40,000 characters moves the head cap's reach from 10% of the payload to 20%
changed.now: Doubling the cap to 40,000 characters moves the head cap's reach from 5% of the payload to 10%
changed.why: 20,000 / 400,110 = 4.9986% and 40,000 / 400,110 = 9.9973%, so the doubling moves the reach from 5% to 10%; the article's own tail-cap sentence already described its 20,000-character span as 'its last 5%', so the old figures contradicted the paragraph two screens above. The following clause is unaffected: 0.62 x 400,110 = 248,068 characters, far outside a 40,000-character head cap. research/agent-tool-result-truncation-loss-2026-review.json source check 14 marked the old wording 'unsupported' and asked for exactly this correction.
